reference: Agius, S.L., & Fox, B.L. (2015). Rapidly cured out-of-autoclave laminates: understanding and controlling the effect of voids on laminate fracture toughness. Composites Part A: Applied Science and Manufacturing, 73, 186-194.
data_source: Abstract (values stated in the text); the full text was not available

material.matrix: out-of-autoclave prepreg resin (not named in the abstract)

G_IIc.test_standard: mode II fracture test (not named in the abstract)

notes: From the abstract: conditioned prepreg gave 'consistently low levels of voids (<0.3%)', non-conditioned laminates 1.5 %, and 'Mode II fracture testing revealed a 21% improvement in toughness for the non-voided laminates', so G_IIc(1.5 %) / G_IIc(< 0.3 %) = 1 / 1.21 = 0.8264. The low-void group is stored at its stated upper bound, 0.3 %; with the true value between 0 and 0.3 % the two-point exponent ln(1.21) / dVp lies between 12.7 and 15.9. Absolute toughness, fibre and resin system, layup, test method and starter crack are in the full text, which was not read.
